```python
from manim import *

class SimplicialComplexScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Unveiling Simplicial Complexes: The Euler Dance", font_size=28)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(title.animate.to_edge(UP).scale(0.7))
        
        # Create a triangle (simplest simplicial complex)
        triangle = Polygon(
            [-2, -1, 0], [2, -1, 0], [0, 2, 0],
            color=BLUE,
            fill_opacity=0.5
        )
        
        # Labels for counts
        v_label = Text("V = 3", font_size=24).to_edge(LEFT).shift(UP*2)
        e_label = Text("E = 3", font_size=24).next_to(v_label, DOWN)
        f_label = Text("F = 1", font_size=24).next_to(e_label, DOWN)
        
        # Euler formula
        euler_formula = MathTex(r"\chi = V - E + F = 3 - 3 + 1 = 1", font_size=28)
        euler_formula.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1)
        
        # Animate triangle and counts
        self.play(Create(triangle))
        self.play(Write(v_label), Write(e_label), Write(f_label))
        self.play(Write(euler_formula))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Text explaining addition of vertex
        add_text = Text("Adding a vertex...", font_size=24)
        add_text.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(add_text))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(add_text))
        
        # Add a new vertex
        new_vertex_pos = [0, -2, 0]
        new_vertex = Dot(new_vertex_pos, color=RED)
        
        # New edges connecting to the new vertex
        new_edge1 = Line([-2, -1, 0], new_vertex_pos, color=GREEN)
        new_edge2 = Line([2, -1, 0], new_vertex_pos, color=GREEN)
        
        # New triangle formed with the new vertex
        new_triangle = Polygon(
            [-2, -1, 0], [2, -1, 0], new_vertex_pos,
            color=BLUE,
            fill_opacity=0.5
        )
        
        # Updated count labels
        new_v_label = Text("V = 4", font_size=24).to_edge(LEFT).shift(UP*2)
        new_e_label = Text("E = 5", font_size=24).next_to(new_v_label, DOWN)
        new_f_label = Text("F = 2", font_size=24).next_to(new_e_label, DOWN)
        
        # Updated Euler formula
        new_euler_formula = MathTex(r"\chi = V - E + F = 4 - 5 + 2 = 1", font_size=28)
        new_euler_formula.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1)
        
        # Animate the addition
        self.play(Create(new_vertex))
        self.play(Create(new_edge1), Create(new_edge2))
        self.play(Create(new_triangle))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Update the counts and formula
        self.play(
            Transform(v_label, new_v_label),
            Transform(e_label, new_e_label),
            Transform(f_label, new_f_label),
            Transform(euler_formula, new_euler_formula)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Text explaining vertex removal
        remove_text = Text("Removing a vertex...", font_size=24)
        remove_text.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(remove_text))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(remove_text))
        
        # Remove all objects and show a new configuration
        self.play(FadeOut(triangle), FadeOut(new_triangle), 
                 FadeOut(new_edge1), FadeOut(new_edge2), FadeOut(new_vertex))
        
        # Create a new triangle (different from original but same Euler characteristic)
        final_triangle = Polygon(
            [2, -1, 0], [0, 2, 0], [0, -2, 0],
            color=BLUE,
            fill_opacity=0.5
        )
        
        self.play(Create(final_triangle))
        
        # Updated count labels after removal
        final_v_label = Text("V = 3", font_size=24).to_edge(LEFT).shift(UP*2)
        final_e_label = Text("E = 3", font_size=24).next_to(final_v_label, DOWN)
        final_f_label = Text("F = 1", font_size=24).next_to(final_e_label, DOWN)
        
        # Final Euler formula
        final_euler_formula = MathTex(r"\chi = V - E + F = 3 - 3 + 1 = 1", font_size=28)
        final_euler_formula.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(v_label, final_v_label),
            Transform(e_label, final_e_label),
            Transform(f_label, final_f_label),
            Transform(euler_formula, final_euler_formula)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Conclusion
        conclusion = Text("The Euler characteristic remains constant: χ = 1", 
                          font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        conclusion.move_to([0, 0, 0])
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final fade out
        self.play(FadeOut(*self.mobjects))
        self.wait(1)
```

```python
        chaos_text = Text("Chaos", color=RED).scale(0.7).to_edge(RIGHT).shift(UP)

        # Create a central attractor point
        attractor_point = Dot(point=axes.c2p(0, 0), color=BLUE, radius=0.1)
        self.play(Create(attractor_point))
        
        # Create stable points (converging to attractor)
        stable_points = [
            axes.c2p(-0.5, 0.5),
            axes.c2p(-0.7, -0.3),
            axes.c2p(0.4, 0.6),
            axes.c2p(0.6, -0.4),
            axes.c2p(-0.2, -0.8)
        ]
        
        stable_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=p, color=BLUE, radius=0.05) for p in stable_points])
        self.play(Create(stable_dots))
        
        # Create chaotic points (diverging)
        chaotic_points = [
            axes.c2p(1.2, 0.5),
            axes.c2p(1.5, -0.3),
            axes.c2p(-1.4, 0.6),
            axes.c2p(-1.6, -0.4),
            axes.c2p(1.2, -0.8)
        ]
        
        chaotic_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=p, color=RED, radius=0.05) for p in chaotic_points])
        self.play(Create(chaotic_dots))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show convergence of stable points to attractor
        stable_dots_target = VGroup(*[Dot(point=axes.c2p(0, 0), color=BLUE, radius=0.05) 
                                   for _ in range(len(stable_points))])
        
        self.play(Transform(stable_dots, stable_dots_target))
        
        # Show divergence of chaotic points
        chaotic_dots_target = VGroup(*[Dot(point=axes.c2p(p[0]*2, p[1]*2, 0), color=RED, radius=0.05) 
                                    for p in chaotic_points])
        
        self.play(Transform(chaotic_dots, chaotic_dots_target))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Create a simple Julia Set boundary
        self.play(
            FadeOut(stable_dots), 
            FadeOut(chaotic_dots),
            FadeOut(attractor_point)
        )
        
        boundary_text = Text("Julia Set Boundary", font_size=24).next_to(eq, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(boundary_text))
        
        # Create a simplified Julia Set boundary using a deformed circle
        n_points = 20
        deformed_circle = []

            # Add some fractal-like perturbation

        # Conclusion

            FadeOut(boundary_text),

            FadeOut(complex_plane),
            FadeOut(eq),
            FadeOut(attractor_text),

        conclusion = Text("Julia Sets: Windows into structured infinity", font_size=24)

        self.play(FadeOut(conclusion))
```

```python
from manim import *

class MinimaxVisualization(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Introduction
        title = Text("Exploring Strategic Moves: Visualizing the Minimax Theorem")
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(title.animate.to_edge(UP).scale(0.7))
        
        # Start with a chessboard
        chessboard = Square(side_length=4).set_fill(GRAY, opacity=0.2)
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(-2, 3):
            h_line = Line(np.array([-2, i, 0]), np.array([2, i, 0]))
            v_line = Line(np.array([i, -2, 0]), np.array([i, 2, 0]))
            grid_lines.add(h_line, v_line)
        
        chessboard_with_grid = VGroup(chessboard, grid_lines)
        chess_text = Text("Strategic Game").next_to(chessboard_with_grid, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(chessboard_with_grid), Write(chess_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transform to a strategy space polygon (simplified polytope)
        polygon = RegularPolygon(n=6, color=BLUE).scale(2)
        polygon.set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.1)
        polytope_text = Text("Strategy Space").next_to(polygon, DOWN)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(chessboard_with_grid, polygon),
            Transform(chess_text, polytope_text)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Add vertices to represent strategic outcomes
        vertices = VGroup()
        for i in range(6):
            angle = i * TAU / 6
            x = 2 * np.cos(angle)
            y = 2 * np.sin(angle)
            vertex = Dot([x, y, 0], color=RED)
            vertices.add(vertex)
        
        vertex_text = Text("Strategic Outcomes").next_to(polygon, DOWN)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(chess_text))
        self.play(Create(vertices))
        self.play(Write(vertex_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show minimax equation
        self.play(FadeOut(vertex_text))
        
        minimax_eq = Tex("min-max = max-min")  # Simplified equation for better compatibility
        self.play(Write(minimax_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show Nash equilibrium at center
        self.play(minimax_eq.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        center_point = Dot(ORIGIN, color=YELLOW).scale(1.5)
        eq_text = Text("Nash Equilibrium").next_to(center_point, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(center_point))
        self.play(Write(eq_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Draw paths from vertices to center
        paths = VGroup()
        for vertex in vertices:
            path = Line(vertex.get_center(), ORIGIN, color=YELLOW)
            paths.add(path)
        
        self.play(Create(paths))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Conclusion
        conclusion = Text("Game Theory: Where Geometry Meets Strategy")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(chessboard_with_grid),
            FadeOut(vertices),
            FadeOut(center_point),
            FadeOut(eq_text),
            FadeOut(paths),
            FadeOut(minimax_eq),
            FadeOut(title)
        )
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
```

```python
        self.interval_line = Line(self.number_line.n2p(-2), self.number_line.n2p(2), color=YELLOW).set_stroke(width=6).shift(UP * 0.1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(self.number_line),

        mid_dot = Dot(self.number_line.n2p(0), color=GREEN)
        mid_label = MathTex("0", color=GREEN).next_to(mid_dot, UP)
        sub_line = Line(self.number_line.n2p(0), self.number_line.n2p(2), color=GREEN).set_stroke(width=8).shift(UP * 0.2)

    def show_1d_combine(self):
```

```python
import numpy as np

class LocusEquidistant(ForgeScene):

    @beat(
        "Introduce two fixed points A and B, and show a point moving such that its distance to both is equal.",
        seconds=3,
        narration="Suppose we have two fixed points in the plane, A and B. What is the locus of points that remain equidistant from both?"
    )
    def show_setup_and_locus(self):
        # Define fixed points
        self.point_a = Dot(color=BLUE).shift(LEFT * 3)
        self.point_b = Dot(color=BLUE).shift(RIGHT * 3)
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=28, color=BLUE).next_to(self.point_a, DOWN)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=28, color=BLUE).next_to(self.point_b, DOWN)
        
        fixed_group = VGroup(self.point_a, self.point_b, label_a, label_b)
        self.play(FadeIn(fixed_group, shift=UP * 0.2), run_time=1)

        # Locus line (Perpendicular bisector)
        self.locus_line = Line(UP * 3.5, DOWN * 3.5, color=YELLOW)
        
        # Tracing point P moving along the locus
        tracker = ValueTracker(-3)
        
        def get_p_pos(t):
            # Move P along the perpendicular bisector (x = 0)
            return np.array([0, t, 0])

        dot_p = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(get_p_pos(tracker.get_value())))
        label_p = always_redraw(lambda: Text("P", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).next_to(dot_p.get_center(), UP + RIGHT * 0.2))
        
        # Distance lines PA and PB
        line_pa = always_redraw(lambda: Line(self.point_a.get_center(), dot_p.get_center(), color=GRAY, stroke_width=2))
        line_pb = always_redraw(lambda: Line(self.point_b.get_center(), dot_p.get_center(), color=GRAY, stroke_width=2))

        self.add(dot_p, label_p, line_pa, line_pb)
```

```python
from manim import *
from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
import numpy as np

class PendulumLinearization(ForgeScene):

    @beat(
        "Introduce the pendulum and show its restoring force",
        seconds=3,
        narration="A pendulum swings under gravity. Its motion is governed by the restoring force, which depends on the sine of the angle."
    )
    def show_pendulum(self):
        # Setup coordinates for pivot and bob
        self.pivot = np.array([-2, 1.5, 0])
        self.length = 2.5
        
        # Draw pivot point
        pivot_dot = Dot(self.pivot, color=WHITE)
        
        # Rod and bob at an angle theta = 60 degrees (0.5 * PI)
        theta = np.pi / 3
        bob_pos = self.pivot + self.length * np.array([np.sin(theta), -np.cos(theta), 0])
        
        self.rod = Line(self.pivot, bob_pos, color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=4)
        self.bob = Dot(bob_pos, radius=0.25, color=BLUE_C)
        
        # Arc for angle theta
        self.angle_arc = Arc(
            radius=0.8,
            start_angle=-np.pi/2,
            angle=-theta,
            arc_center=self.pivot,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.angle_label = MathTex(r"\theta", color=YELLOW).next_to(self.angle_arc, DOWN + RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Force vector (tangential component proportional to sin(theta))
        force_start = bob_pos
        force_end = force_start + 1.2 * np.array([np.cos(theta), np.sin(theta), 0])
        self.force_vector = Arrow(force_start, force_end, color=RED, buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        self.force_label = MathTex(r"-mg \sin(\theta)", color=RED).next_to(self.force_vector, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # Equations on the right side
        self.eq_group = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"\frac{d^2\theta}{dt^2} + \frac{g}{L} \sin(\theta) = 0", font_size=36),
        ).to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1.0).shift(UP * 1.5)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(pivot_dot),
            Create(self.rod),
            FadeIn(self.bob),
            Create(self.angle_arc),
            Write(self.angle_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(self.force_vector),
            Write(self.force_label),
            Write(self.eq_group),
            run_time=1.5
        )

    @beat(
        "Show the small angle approximation where sine of theta equals theta",
        seconds=3,
        narration="For very small angles, the sine of theta is approximately equal to theta itself, turning a messy nonlinear equation into simple harmonic motion."
    )
    def linearize(self):
        # Replacement equation emphasizing the approximation
        approx_eq = MathTex(r"\sin(\theta) \approx \theta", color=YELLOW, font_size=36)
        approx_eq.next_to(self.eq_group, DOWN, buff=0.5)

        simple_eq = MathTex(r"\frac{d^2\theta}{dt^2} + \frac{g}{L} \theta = 0", color=GREEN_C, font_size=36)
        simple_eq.next_to(approx_eq, DOWN, buff=0.5)

        # Swing the pendulum to a smaller angle to visualize linearization
        small_theta = 0.155
        new_bob_pos = self.pivot + self.length * np.array([np.sin(small_theta), -np.cos(small_theta), 0])
        
        new_rod = Line(self.pivot, new_bob_pos, color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=4)
        new_angle_arc = Arc(
            radius=0.8,
            start_angle=-np.pi/2,
            angle=-small_theta,
            arc_center=self.pivot,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        new_angle_label = MathTex(r"\theta", color=YELLOW).next_to(new_angle_arc, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        new_force_end = new_bob_pos + 1.2 * np.array([np.cos(small_theta), np.sin(small_theta), 0])
        new_force_vector = Arrow(new_bob_pos, new_force_end, color=RED, buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        new_force_label = MathTex(r"-mg \theta", color=RED).next_to(new_force_vector, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            Transform(self.rod, new_rod),
            self.bob.animate.move_to(new_bob_pos),
            Transform(self.angle_arc, new_angle_arc),
            Transform(self.angle_label, new_angle_label),
            Transform(self.force_vector, new_force_vector),
            Transform(self.force_label, new_force_label),
            Write(approx_eq),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            Write(simple_eq),
            run_time=1.5
        )
```

```python
class FundamentalTheoremOfCalculus(ForgeScene):
    @beat("Introduce the coordinate plane and a smooth curve representing a function.", seconds=4, narration="Imagine a continuous function, tracing out a curve on the plane. We want to understand how the accumulation of area under this curve relates to the curve itself.")
    def intro(self):
        self.axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=6,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"color": BLUE_E, "stroke_width": 2}
        ).shift(LEFT * 1.5 + DOWN * 0.5)

        self.curve = self.axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x) + 0.2 * x + 1, x_range=[0, 5.5], color=YELLOW)
        self.func_label = MathTex("f(t)", color=YELLOW).next_to(self.curve.get_top(), UP)

        self.play(Create(self.axes), Create(self.curve), Write(self.func_label), run_time=3.5)

    @beat("Define the accumulation function as an area from a fixed point to variable x.", seconds=5, narration="Let's define a new function: the accumulated area under the curve from a starting point up to some variable point x.")
    def define_area(self):
        self.x_val = 3.5
        # Compute underlying function value correctly for plotting top edge of area
        f_func = lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x) + 0.2 * x + 1
        self.area = self.axes.get_area(self.curve, x_range=[0, self.x_val], color=BLUE, opacity=0.4)
        
        self.x_line = DashedLine(
            start=self.axes.c2p(self.x_val, 0),
            end=self.axes.c2p(self.x_val, f_func(self.x_val)),
            color=WHITE,
            dash_length=0.1
        )
        self.x_label = MathTex("x", color=WHITE).next_to(self.x_line, DOWN)

        self.area_label = MathTex("A(x) = \\int_{0}^{x} f(t)\\,dt", color=BLUE_C).to_edge(RIGHT).shift(UP * 1.5)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.area), Create(self.x_line), Write(self.x_label), Write(self.area_label), run_time=4)

    @beat("Show what happens when we add a small sliver of width dx to x.", seconds=5, narration="Now, what happens if we push x forward by a tiny bit, delta x? We add a thin vertical strip of area under the curve.")
    def add_sliver(self):
        self.dx = 0.8
        f_func = lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x) + 0.2 * x + 1
        self.sliver = self.axes.get_area(
            self.curve, 
            x_range=[self.x_val, self.x_val + self.dx], 
            color=GREEN, 
            opacity=0.7
        )
        
        self.x_plus_dx_line = DashedLine(
            start=self.axes.c2p(self.x_val + self.dx, 0),
            end=self.axes.c2p(self.x_val + self.dx, f_func(self.x_val + self.dx)),
            color=GREEN,
            dash_length=0.1
        )
        self.dx_label = MathTex("x + dx", color=GREEN).next_to(self.x_plus_dx_line, DOWN)
        self.sliver_label = MathTex("dA", color=GREEN).move_to(self.axes.c2p(self.x_val + self.dx / 2, 1.5))

        self.play(
            FadeIn(self.sliver), 
            Create(self.x_plus_dx_line), 
            Transform(self.x_label, self.dx_label),
            Write(self.sliver_label),
            run_time=4.5
        )

    @beat("Approximate the sliver area as a rectangle of height f(x) and width dx.", seconds=5, narration="Since the width delta x is extremely small, this sliver is roughly a rectangle. Its area is simply its height, f of x, times its width, delta x.")
    def rect_approximation(self):
        self.rect = self.axes.get_riemann_rectangles(
            self.curve, 
            x_range=[self.x_val, self.x_val + self.dx], 
            dx=self.dx,
            color=GREEN_A, 
            fill_opacity=0.5
        )
        
        self.formula_approx = MathTex("dA \\approx f(x) \\cdot dx", color=GREEN_C).next_to(self.area_label, DOWN, buff=0.5)

        self.play(
            Transform(self.sliver, self.rect),
            Write(self.formula_approx),
            run_time=4
        )

    @beat("Rearrange the equation to express the rate of change of area.", seconds=5, narration="If we divide both sides by delta x, we get an expression for the average rate at which the area is growing.")
    def rearrange(self):
        self.formula_div = MathTex("\\frac{dA}{dx} \\approx f(x)", color=WHITE).next_to(self.formula_approx, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(
            TransformMatchingTex(self.formula_approx.copy(), self.formula_div),
            run_time=4
        )

    @beat("Take the limit as dx approaches zero to get an exact derivative.", seconds=5, narration="As delta x shrinks down to zero, this approximation becomes exact. The derivative of the accumulated area function is precisely the original function.")
    def take_limit(self):
        self.formula_exact = MathTex("\\frac{d}{dx} \\left[ \\int_{0}^{x} f(t)\\,dt \\right] = f(x)", color=YELLOW).move_to(self.formula_div.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(self.sliver_label),
            Transform(self.formula_div, self.formula_exact),
            run_time=4
        )

    @beat("Connect this back to antiderivatives to state the full theorem.", seconds=5, narration="This is the beating heart of calculus: integration and differentiation are inverse operations. Finding the area under a curve is the exact opposite of finding its slope.")
    def full_theorem(self):
        self.box = SurroundingRectangle(self.formula_exact, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
        
        self.ftc_statement = MathTex("A'(x) = f(x)", color=GREEN_C).to_edge(RIGHT).shift(DOWN * 1.5)

        self.play(
            Create(self.box),
            Write(self.ftc_statement),
            run_time=4
        )

    @beat("Summarize the fundamental theorem visually across the board.", seconds=4, narration="Area under the curve and the slope of the curve. Two seemingly unrelated geometric concepts, locked together by the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.")
    def summary(self):
        self.play(
            self.area.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.6),
            self.curve.animate.set_color(GREEN),
            run_time=3.5
        )

    @beat("Clean up and conclude the scene.", seconds=3, narration="And that is how the bridge between geometry and analysis is built.")
    def outro(self):
        self.play(
            FadeOut(self.axes),
            FadeOut(self.curve),
            FadeOut(self.area),
            FadeOut(self.x_line),
            FadeOut(self.x_plus_dx_line),
            FadeOut(self.x_label),
            FadeOut(self.func_label),
            FadeOut(self.area_label),
            FadeOut(self.formula_div),
            FadeOut(self.box),
            FadeOut(self.ftc_statement),

        )
```

```python
class BasicDefiniteIntegral(Scene):

        self.play(Write(problem))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show the integral bounds

        self.play(Write(bounds))

        self.wait(2)
        
        # Apply the bounds
```

```python
    def show_parameter(self):
```

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class MonteCarloPI(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Create the title
        title = Text("Dancing with Randomness: Estimating π with Monte Carlo")
        title.set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title))
        
        # Create the square and circle
        square = Square(side_length=4, color=BLUE_C).shift(LEFT * 2.5)
        circle = Circle(radius=2, color=GREEN_C).shift(LEFT * 2.5)
        
        self.play(Create(square), Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Initialize counters
        points_inside = 0
        total_points = 0
        
        # Display counters
        inside_text = Text(f"Points inside: {points_inside}", font_size=24, color=GREEN_C).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 1.5)
        total_text = Text(f"Total points: {total_points}", font_size=24, color=BLUE_C).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 1)
        pi_estimate_text = Text(f"π estimate: 0", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(inside_text), Write(total_text), Write(pi_estimate_text))
        
        # Generate random points
        num_points = 30  # For a shorter animation
        
        for i in range(num_points):
            # Generate a random point within the square
            x = np.random.uniform(-2, 2)
            y = np.random.uniform(-2, 2)
            
            # Check if the point is inside the circle
            inside_circle = x**2 + y**2 <= 4  # Circle has radius 2
            
            if inside_circle:
                points_inside += 1
                point_color = GREEN_C
            else:
                point_color = ORANGE
            
            total_points += 1
            
            # Create a point at the random location
            point = Dot(point=np.array([x, y, 0]) + LEFT * 2.5, color=point_color)
            
            # Update the counters
            new_inside_text = Text(f"Points inside: {points_inside}", font_size=24, color=GREEN_C).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 1.5)
            new_total_text = Text(f"Total points: {total_points}", font_size=24, color=BLUE_C).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 1)
            pi_estimate = 4 * points_inside / total_points
            new_pi_estimate_text = Text(f"π estimate: {pi_estimate:.4f}", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 0.5)
            
            # Animate the addition of the point and update the counters
            self.play(
                Create(point),
                Transform(inside_text, new_inside_text),
                Transform(total_text, new_total_text),
                Transform(pi_estimate_text, new_pi_estimate_text),
                run_time=0.1  # Fast animation
            )
        
        # Show the actual value of pi
        actual_pi = Text(f"Actual π: {np.pi:.4f}", font_size=24, color=ORANGE).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + DOWN * 1)
        self.play(Write(actual_pi))
        
        # Conclude with the formula
        formula = Text("Estimated π = 4 × (Inside Points / Total Points)", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        formula.scale(0.7).to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)
```

```python
"""Gold scene 011 — a function as a machine, and as a curve.

Tier 1. Two pictures of the same object, and the connection between them is
what every later calculus scene assumes. A model that has only ever seen the
curve will not know the curve is a *record* of something.

Every output shown is computed by calling the function, so the machine's
answers and the plotted curve cannot drift apart.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat

IN_C = "#F0AC5F"
OUT_C = "#5CD0B3"
BOX_C = BLUE_C
DIM = GREY_B


def f(x: float) -> float:
    return 0.5 * x ** 2 - 1.0


class FunctionMachine(ForgeScene):

    samples = [-2.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0]

    @beat("A machine that takes a number and returns one", seconds=13,
          narration="Think of a function as a machine. A number goes in, the "
                    "machine does something to it, and one number comes out. "
                    "The rule here is: square it, halve it, subtract one.")
    def machine(self):
        self.box = RoundedRectangle(width=2.6, height=1.5, corner_radius=0.18,
                                    color=BOX_C, stroke_width=3,
                                    fill_opacity=0.12, fill_color=BOX_C)
        self.box.move_to(LEFT * 3.3 + UP * 0.9)
        rule = MathTex(r"\tfrac{x^2}{2} - 1", font_size=34, color=BOX_C).move_to(self.box)
        self.in_arrow = Arrow(self.box.get_left() + LEFT * 1.1, self.box.get_left(),
                              buff=0.1, color=IN_C, stroke_width=4)
        self.out_arrow = Arrow(self.box.get_right(), self.box.get_right() + RIGHT * 1.1,
                               buff=0.1, color=OUT_C, stroke_width=4)
        self.title = Text("Two pictures of the same thing",
                          font_size=29).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)
        self.play(Create(self.box), Write(rule), run_time=1.3)
        self.play(GrowArrow(self.in_arrow), GrowArrow(self.out_arrow), run_time=0.9)
        self.wait(0.8)

    @beat("Feed it numbers and watch what comes out", seconds=15,
          narration="Put in minus two, and four comes back — no, one. Put in "
                    "zero and you get minus one. Each input produces exactly "
                    "one output. That is the whole requirement: never two "
                    "answers for the same question.")
    def feed(self):
        self.rows = VGroup()
        for x in self.samples:
            y = f(x)                    # computed, never typed
            lab_in = MathTex(f"{x:g}", font_size=30, color=IN_C)
            lab_in.next_to(self.in_arrow, LEFT, buff=0.15)
            lab_out = MathTex(f"{y:g}", font_size=30, color=OUT_C)
            lab_out.next_to(self.out_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.15)
            self.play(FadeIn(lab_in, shift=RIGHT * 0.2), run_time=0.35)
            self.play(Indicate(self.box, color=BOX_C, scale_factor=1.06), run_time=0.35)
            self.play(FadeIn(lab_out, shift=RIGHT * 0.2), run_time=0.35)
            self.rows.add(VGroup(
                MathTex(rf"{x:g} \;\mapsto\; {y:g}", font_size=26, color=DIM)))
            self.play(FadeOut(lab_in), FadeOut(lab_out), run_time=0.25)

        self.rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.18).move_to([-3.3, -1.7, 0])
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r) for r in self.rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.15, run_time=1.2))
        self.wait(0.7)

    @beat("Plot each pair as a point", seconds=13,
          narration="Now plot each pair. The input along the bottom, the output "
                    "up the side. Five inputs, five points. Nothing new has "
                    "happened — this is the same list, drawn instead of "
                    "written.")
```

```python
"""Gold scene 019 — the walk that cannot be done.

Graphs, Tier 3. Konigsberg is the scene where an animation can do something a
proof on paper cannot: fail, visibly, several times, before explaining why
failure was guaranteed. Watching three attempts strand themselves is what
makes the counting argument land as an explanation rather than an assertion.

Nothing here is staged. The bridges are a real multigraph -- four of the seven
are doubled pairs, and ``degree`` counts multiplicities, because two bridges
between the same banks are two ways across. The parity argument is run by the
primitive: four land masses are odd, a walk has two ends, so no such walk
exists. ``verify_konigsberg_has_no_walk`` asserts it before the scene says it.

The attempted routes are checked too: each is a genuine walk along real
bridges that genuinely runs out, not a path drawn to look stuck.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.graphs import (KONIGSBERG, euler_path_exists,
                                     odd_degree_nodes, verify_walk_strands,
                                     verify_konigsberg_has_no_walk,
                                     walk_until_stuck)

LAND_C = "#8D7350"
WATER_C = "#2A4A63"
BRIDGE_C = GREY_B
WALK_C = "#5CD0B3"
STUCK_C = "#FC6255"
ODD_C = "#F0AC5F"
DIM = GREY_B

LAYOUT = LEFT * 2.6
SC = 1.15

#: Which of the seven bridges runs where. Parallel bridges are bowed apart by
#: ``bend`` so both are visible; they are the same connection either way.
BRIDGES = [("N", "A", -0.45), ("N", "A", 0.45),
           ("S", "A", -0.45), ("S", "A", 0.45),
           ("N", "B", 0.0), ("S", "B", 0.0), ("A", "B", 0.0)]

NAMES = {"N": "north bank", "A": "the island", "B": "east quarter",
         "S": "south bank"}

# walk_until_stuck returns indices into KONIGSBERG.edges, and the scene
# looks them up in BRIDGES. The two lists must stay in lockstep.
assert [(a, b) for a, b, _ in BRIDGES] == \
       [(a, b) for a, b, _ in KONIGSBERG.edges]


class Konigsberg(ForgeScene):

    def pos(self, n):
        x, y = KONIGSBERG.nodes[n]
        return LAYOUT + np.array([x * SC, y * SC, 0.0])

    def bridge(self, a, b, bend):
        start, end = self.pos(a), self.pos(b)
        if abs(bend) < 1e-9:
            return Line(start, end, color=BRIDGE_C, stroke_width=4)
        return ArcBetweenPoints(start, end, angle=bend * 2,
                                color=BRIDGE_C, stroke_width=4)

    def panel(self, *rows):
        g = VGroup(*rows).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        return g.move_to(RIGHT * 3.9).align_to(UP * 2.4, UP)

    @beat("Four pieces of land, seven bridges", seconds=17,
          narration="Konigsberg, seventeen thirty-six. A river splits the "
                    "city into four pieces: two banks, an island, and a "
                    "quarter to the east. Seven bridges join them. The "
                    "townspeople asked a question that sounds like a puzzle "
                    "and turned out to start a branch of mathematics.")
    def city(self):
        self.title = Text("The seven bridges of Konigsberg",
                          font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)

        self.lands, self.land_labels = {}, {}
        blobs = VGroup()
        for n in KONIGSBERG.nodes:
            c = Circle(radius=0.42, color=LAND_C, fill_color=LAND_C,
                       fill_opacity=0.45, stroke_width=3).move_to(self.pos(n))
            t = Text(n, font_size=24, color=WHITE).move_to(c)
            self.lands[n], self.land_labels[n] = c, t
            blobs.add(VGroup(c, t))

        self.spans = []
        arcs = VGroup()
        for a, b, bend in BRIDGES:
            arc = self.bridge(a, b, bend)
            self.spans.append(((a, b), arc))
            arcs.add(arc)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b, scale=0.6) for b in blobs],
                              lag_ratio=0.15, run_time=1.4))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(a) for a in arcs],
                              lag_ratio=0.16, run_time=2.4))

        legend = self.panel(*[
            VGroup(Text(k, font_size=22, color=LAND_C),
                   Text(NAMES[k], font_size=19, color=DIM)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
            for k in ("N", "A", "B", "S")])
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in legend],
                              lag_ratio=0.2, run_time=1.4))
        self.legend = legend
        self.wait(1.0)

    @beat("The question, and three honest attempts", seconds=27,
          narration="Can you walk through the city crossing every bridge "
                    "exactly once? Try it. Start on the north bank and you "
                    "strand yourself with a bridge still unused. Start on the "
                    "island instead — stranded again. Start in the east "
                    "quarter and you barely get going. Something is always "
                    "left over, and no amount of trying tells you whether you "
                    "are unlucky or whether it cannot be done at all.")
    def attempts(self):
        question = Text("cross every bridge exactly once?",
                        font_size=24, color=WALK_C).next_to(
            self.title, DOWN, buff=0.35)
        self.play(FadeIn(question), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.legend), run_time=0.4)

        # The routes are walked, not written. Three attempts drafted by eye
        # turned out to be one illegal walk and two that could have carried
        # on: the narration said "stranded" and the bridges disagreed. Every
        # maximal walk here strands, because no Euler path exists -- so the
        # plain edge order is enough, and each one is checked before it plays.
        self.tally = None
        for start_node in ("N", "A", "B"):
            walk = walk_until_stuck(KONIGSBERG, start_node)
            assert verify_walk_strands(KONIGSBERG, walk, start_node)

            used = VGroup()
            marker = Dot(self.pos(start_node), color=WALK_C, radius=0.11)
            self.play(FadeIn(marker, scale=0.5), run_time=0.35)
            for step in walk:
                arc = self.spans[step.edge_index][1]
                self.play(arc.animate.set_stroke(WALK_C, width=6),
                          marker.animate.move_to(self.pos(step.to)),
                          run_time=0.4)
                used.add(arc)

            left = len(BRIDGES) - len(walk)
            msg = Text(f"{left} bridge{'s' if left != 1 else ''} unused",
                       font_size=22, color=STUCK_C).next_to(
                question, DOWN, buff=0.45)
            if self.tally is None:
                self.play(FadeIn(msg), run_time=0.5)
            else:
                self.play(FadeTransform(self.tally, msg), run_time=0.5)
            self.tally = msg
            self.play(Flash(marker, color=STUCK_C, line_length=0.2,
                            flash_radius=0.34, num_lines=10), run_time=0.6)
            self.play(FadeOut(marker),
                      *[a.animate.set_stroke(BRIDGE_C, width=4) for a in used],
                      run_time=0.5)
        self.question = question
        self.wait(0.8)

    @beat("Throw the map away and keep the connections", seconds=26,
          narration="Euler's move was to stop looking at the map. The shape "
                    "of the island does not matter, nor the length of any "
                    "bridge, nor which way the river bends. The only thing "
                    "that decides the answer is which pieces of land are "
                    "joined, and by how many bridges. Shrink each piece of "
                    "land to a dot and the whole problem is four dots and "
                    "seven lines.")
    def abstract(self):
        self.play(FadeOut(self.question), FadeOut(self.tally), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(*[c.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.0).scale(0.62)
                    for c in self.lands.values()],
                  *[t.animate.scale(0.82) for t in self.land_labels.values()],
                  run_time=1.6)

        counts = {n: KONIGSBERG.degree(n) for n in KONIGSBERG.nodes}
        assert sum(counts.values()) == 2 * len(BRIDGES)   # handshake lemma

        rows = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(Text(n, font_size=22, color=LAND_C),
                   Text("touches", font_size=18, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{counts[n]}", font_size=28, color=ODD_C),
                   Text("bridges", font_size=18, color=DIM),
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.22)
            for n in ("N", "A", "B", "S")])
        rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.28, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        total = VGroup(
            MathTex(rf"{sum(counts.values())}", font_size=26, color=DIM),
            Text("ends, for 7 bridges", font_size=18, color=DIM),
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.22)
        self.degrees = self.panel(rows, total)

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.28, run_time=1.8))
        self.play(FadeIn(total), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(1.2)

    @beat("Count the odd ones, and the answer is forced", seconds=29,
          narration="Here is the argument. Any piece of land you pass through "
                    "costs two bridges — one to arrive, one to leave. So a "
                    "land touched by an odd number of bridges can only be "
                    "where you start or where you finish. A walk has two "
                    "ends. But every one of these four is odd: five, three, "
                    "three, three. Four candidates for two positions. The "
                    "walk does not exist, and no cleverness will find it.")
    def parity(self):
        assert verify_konigsberg_has_no_walk()
        odd = odd_degree_nodes(KONIGSBERG)
        assert not euler_path_exists(KONIGSBERG)
        assert len(odd) == 4
        # the narration says "five, three, three, three"
        assert sorted(KONIGSBERG.degree(n) for n in KONIGSBERG.nodes) \
            == [3, 3, 3, 5]

        self.play(FadeOut(self.degrees), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[
            self.lands[n].animate.set_stroke(ODD_C, width=5) for n in odd],
            lag_ratio=0.2, run_time=1.4))

        rule = self.panel(
            Text("pass through a land", font_size=20, color=DIM),
            Text("= 2 bridges", font_size=22, color=WALK_C),
            Text("odd land = an end", font_size=20, color=ODD_C),
            Text("a walk has 2 ends", font_size=20, color=DIM),
        )
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rule],
                              lag_ratio=0.35, run_time=2.2))
        self.wait(1.4)

        verdict = VGroup(
            VGroup(MathTex(rf"{len(odd)}", font_size=40, color=ODD_C),
                   Text("odd lands", font_size=21, color=DIM)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            Text("more than 2", font_size=22, color=STUCK_C),
            Text("no such walk exists", font_size=26, color=STUCK_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        verdict.next_to(rule, DOWN, buff=0.6).align_to(rule, LEFT)

        self.play(FadeIn(verdict[0], shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(verdict[1]), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Write(verdict[2]), run_time=1.2)
        self.wait(2.4)
```

```python
from manim import *
from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
import numpy as np

class FractalBoundaryCorrection(ForgeScene):

    @beat("So maybe you go and try to add even smaller blobs, with the relevant third color around those smaller boundaries to help try to correct.", seconds=4, narration="So maybe you go and try to add even smaller blobs, with the relevant third color around those smaller boundaries to help try to correct.")
    def add_initial_blobs(self):
        self.main_region = Circle(radius=2.0, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3).to_edge(LEFT, buff=1.0)
        self.main_label = Text("Original Blob", font_size=24, color=BLUE).next_to(self.main_region, UP)
        
        # Smaller blobs around the boundary
        angles = np.linspace(0, 2*PI, 6, endpoint=False)
        self.small_blobs = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.4, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(
                self.main_region.get_center() + np.array([2.0 * np.cos(a), 2.0 * np.sin(a), 0])
            ) for a in angles
        ])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(self.main_region), Write(self.main_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromCenter(b) for b in self.small_blobs], lag_ratio=0.1), run_time=2.0)

    @beat("And likewise you have to do this for every one of the blobs that you initially added.", seconds=4, narration="And likewise you have to do this for every one of the blobs that you initially added.")
    def multiply_blobs(self):
        # Even smaller blobs attached to the previous ones
        self.tiny_blobs = VGroup()
```

```python
        self.play(Create(firm2), Write(firm2_label))
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Part 3: Convergence to Nash Equilibrium
        self.play(
            FadeOut(firm1), FadeOut(firm2),
            FadeOut(firm1_label), FadeOut(firm2_label),
            FadeOut(arrow)
        )
        self.play(Transform(header, Text("Nash Equilibrium", font_size=36).to_edge(UP)))
        
        # Nash point with arrows converging

        nash_label = Text("Equilibrium", font_size=20)
        nash_label.next_to(nash_point, DOWN)
        
        # Four arrows pointing to Nash equilibrium
        arrows = VGroup()
        for angle in [0, PI/2, PI, 3*PI/2]:
            start_x = 2 * np.cos(angle)
            start_y = 2 * np.sin(angle)
            arrow = Arrow([start_x, start_y, 0], [0, 0, 0], color=YELLOW)
            arrows.add(arrow)
        
        self.play(Create(arrows))
        self.play(Create(nash_point))
        self.play(Write(nash_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Simple heatmap visualization
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arrows),
            FadeOut(nash_point),
            FadeOut(nash_label)
        )
        self.play(Transform(header, Text("Strategy Density", font_size=36).to_edge(UP)))

        self.wait(1)
        
        # Part 4: Equation
        self.play(FadeOut(heatmap))
        self.play(Transform(header, Text("Mathematical Representation", font_size=36).to_edge(UP)))

            FadeOut(equation),
            FadeOut(equation_desc)
        )

        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
```

```python
from manim import *
from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
import numpy as np

class CompareAndSwapSort(ForgeScene):
    values = [1.5, 3.8, 2.0, 4.2, 2.9]
    idx1, idx2 = 1, 2  # Indices of adjacent elements to compare

    def get_x(self, index):
        return -3.0 + index * 1.5

    def make_bar(self, val, index, color=BLUE_C):
        rect = Rectangle(
            width=1.0,
            height=val,
            fill_opacity=0.85,
            fill_color=color,
            stroke_color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        pos = np.array([self.get_x(index), -1.8 + val / 2.0, 0])
        rect.move_to(pos)
        lbl = DecimalNumber(
            val,
            num_decimal_places=1,
            font_size=24,
            color=WHITE
        ).next_to(rect, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        return VGroup(rect, lbl)

    @beat("Compare adjacent elements in array", seconds=3)
    def compare_elements(self):
        self.bars = VGroup(*[
            self.make_bar(val, i) for i, val in enumerate(self.values)
        ])

        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b, shift=UP * 0.3) for b in self.bars], lag_ratio=0.1),
            run_time=1.2
        )

        v1, v2 = self.values[self.idx1], self.values[self.idx2]
        needs_swap = v1 > v2  # dynamically evaluated condition

        highlight1 = self.make_bar(v1, self.idx1, color=RED_C)
        highlight2 = self.make_bar(v2, self.idx2, color=RED_C)

        comp_op = ">" if needs_swap else "≤"
        action = "Swap Needed" if needs_swap else "In Order"
        self.cmp_text = Text(
            f"{v1} {comp_op} {v2}  ({action})",
            font_size=28,
            color=RED_C
        ).to_edge(UP, buff=0.8)

        self.play(
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx1], highlight1),
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx2], highlight2),
            Write(self.cmp_text),
            run_time=1.3
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

    @beat("Swap out-of-order bars", seconds=3)
    def swap_elements(self):
        v1, v2 = self.values[self.idx1], self.values[self.idx2]

        # Target center locations after swap
        target_pos1 = self.make_bar(v1, self.idx2).get_center()
        target_pos2 = self.make_bar(v2, self.idx1).get_center()

        path1 = ArcBetweenPoints(self.bars[self.idx1].get_center(), target_pos1, angle=-PI / 2)
        path2 = ArcBetweenPoints(self.bars[self.idx2].get_center(), target_pos2, angle=-PI / 2)

        swapped1 = self.make_bar(v1, self.idx2, color=GREEN_C)
        swapped2 = self.make_bar(v2, self.idx1, color=GREEN_C)

        sorted_text = Text(
            f"{v2} < {v1}  (Sorted)",
            font_size=28,
            color=GREEN_C
        ).to_edge(UP, buff=0.8)

        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(self.bars[self.idx1], path1),
            MoveAlongPath(self.bars[self.idx2], path2),
            Transform(self.cmp_text, sorted_text),
            run_time=1.8
        )

        self.play(
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx1], swapped1),
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx2], swapped2),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.wait(0.4)
```

```python
I_C = "#5CD0B3"
J_C = "#F0AC5F"
V_C = BLUE_C
DIM = GREY_B

M = Mat2(2.0, 1.0, 0.0, 3.0)
U = 0.78
CENTRE = LEFT * 1.9 + DOWN * 0.2
PROBE = Vec2(1.5, 0.5)


class LinearTransform(ForgeScene):

    def p(self, v):
        return CENTRE + np.array([v.x * U, v.y * U, 0.0])

    def grid_lines(self, m=None, colour=GRID_C, width=1.4, span=5):

                     stroke_width=width, max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.22)

        return g.move_to(RIGHT * 4.3).align_to(UP * 2.3, UP)

        c1, c2 = M.columns

        self.play(FadeOut(self.note), run_time=0.3)
        target_grid = self.grid_lines(M)
        self.play(Transform(self.grid, target_grid),
                  Transform(self.i_hat, self.arrow(c1, I_C)),
                  Transform(self.j_hat, self.arrow(c2, J_C)),
                  Transform(self.v, self.arrow(M.apply(PROBE), V_C, width=4)),

                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),

                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
            Text("grid stays a grid", font_size=19, color=DIM),

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(n, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for n in note],

    def matrix(self):

        self.play(FadeOut(self.note), run_time=0.3)

        mat = Matrix([[f"{M.a:.0f}", f"{M.b:.0f}"],

        mat.scale(0.9).move_to(RIGHT * 4.2 + UP * 1.7)
        cols = mat.get_columns()
        cols[0].set_color(I_C)
        cols[1].set_color(J_C)
        self.play(Write(mat), run_time=1.6)

        braces = VGroup(
            Text("where i went", font_size=16, color=I_C),
            Text("where j went", font_size=16, color=J_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.16, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        braces.next_to(mat, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(braces, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.9)

        work = VGroup(
            MathTex(rf"{PROBE.x}\,({c1.x:.0f},{c1.y:.0f}) + "
                    rf"{PROBE.y}\,({c2.x:.0f},{c2.y:.0f})",
                    font_size=22, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"= ({M.apply(PROBE).x:.1f}, {M.apply(PROBE).y:.1f})",
                    font_size=26, color=V_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.22, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        work.next_to(braces, DOWN, buff=0.5).align_to(braces, LEFT)
        self.play(Write(work[0]), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(work[1], shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.8)
        self.mat_group = VGroup(mat, braces, work)

          narration="And because a map is fully described by where the two "
                    "vectors land, doing one map and then another is itself "
                    "just a map — you only need to ask where the two end up "
                    "after both. That is what multiplying matrices means. Not "
                    "a rule about rows and columns; a question about where two "
                    "arrows finish.")
    def compose(self):
        N = Mat2(0.0, -1.0, 1.0, 0.0)          # quarter turn
        NM = N @ M
        # Composition must agree with applying the two in order, at real points.
        for pt in (Vec2(1, 0), Vec2(0, 1), PROBE, Vec2(-1.3, 2.1)):
            got = NM.apply(pt)
            want = N.apply(M.apply(pt))
            assert abs(got.x - want.x) < 1e-12 and abs(got.y - want.y) < 1e-12

        self.play(FadeOut(self.mat_group), run_time=0.4)
        c1, c2 = NM.columns
        self.play(Transform(self.grid, self.grid_lines(NM)),
                  Transform(self.i_hat, self.arrow(c1, I_C)),
                  Transform(self.j_hat, self.arrow(c2, J_C)),
                  Transform(self.v, self.arrow(NM.apply(PROBE), V_C, width=4)),
                  run_time=2.6)

        rows = self.panel(
            Text("then a quarter turn", font_size=19, color=DIM),
            VGroup(MathTex(r"\hat{\imath} \to", font_size=22, color=I_C),
                   MathTex(rf"({c1.x:.0f}, {c1.y:.0f})", font_size=22, color=I_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
            VGroup(MathTex(r"\hat{\jmath} \to", font_size=22, color=J_C),
                   MathTex(rf"({c2.x:.0f}, {c2.y:.0f})", font_size=22, color=J_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
            Text("one map, not two", font_size=20, color=V_C),
        )
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.8))
```

```python
"""Gold scene 043 — the determinant is an area factor.

Vectors, Tier 2, building on the transform scene. The formula ad minus bc is
easy to memorise and tells you nothing. What it *is* is the factor by which
every area changes, and the sign is whether the plane got flipped over.

The scene measures rather than asserts. ``verify_det_is_area_factor`` maps two
polygons -- the unit square and a deliberately irregular quadrilateral -- and
compares their shoelace areas before and after. The second shape matters: a
check done only on an axis-aligned square would pass for maps that stretch
correctly and shear wrongly.

The zero case is the payoff. A determinant of zero means every area is
crushed to nothing, the whole plane collapses onto a line, and information is
destroyed -- which is exactly why such a matrix has no inverse.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.vectors import (Mat2, Vec2, polygon_area,
                                      verify_det_is_area_factor)

I_C = "#5CD0B3"
J_C = "#F0AC5F"
AREA_C = BLUE_C
FLIP_C = "#8B7FD4"
ZERO_C = "#FC6255"
DIM = GREY_B

M = Mat2(3.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0)          # det 5
FLIP = Mat2(1.0, 2.0, 2.0, 1.0)       # det -3
SQUASH = Mat2(2.0, 1.0, 4.0, 2.0)     # det 0
U = 0.72
CENTRE = LEFT * 2.0 + DOWN * 0.3
SHAPE = [Vec2(-0.4, -0.2), Vec2(1.3, 0.1), Vec2(0.9, 1.4), Vec2(-0.7, 0.8)]


class Determinant(ForgeScene):

    def p(self, v):
        return CENTRE + np.array([v.x * U, v.y * U, 0.0])

    def unit_square(self, m=None, colour=AREA_C):
        pts = [Vec2(0, 0), Vec2(1, 0), Vec2(1, 1), Vec2(0, 1)]
        if m:
            pts = [m.apply(p) for p in pts]
        return Polygon(*[self.p(p) for p in pts], color=colour,
                       fill_color=colour, fill_opacity=0.32, stroke_width=2.6)

    def blob(self, m=None, colour=FLIP_C):
        pts = [m.apply(p) for p in SHAPE] if m else SHAPE
        return Polygon(*[self.p(p) for p in pts], color=colour,
                       fill_color=colour, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2.2)

    def axes_lines(self):
        g = VGroup()
        for k in range(-6, 7):
            g.add(Line(self.p(Vec2(k, -6)), self.p(Vec2(k, 6)),
                       color=GREY_E, stroke_width=1.1, stroke_opacity=0.5))
            g.add(Line(self.p(Vec2(-6, k)), self.p(Vec2(6, k)),
                       color=GREY_E, stroke_width=1.1, stroke_opacity=0.5))
        return g

    def panel(self, *rows):
        g = VGroup(*rows).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        return g.move_to(RIGHT * 4.3).align_to(UP * 2.3, UP)

    @beat("Start with a square of area one", seconds=15,
          narration="The grid, and the square between the two basis vectors. "
                    "Its area is one, by definition — that square is the unit "
                    "the rest of the plane is measured in. Watch what a "
                    "transformation does to it.")
    def start(self):
        self.title = Text("The determinant is an area factor",
                          font_size=29).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)
        self.grid = self.axes_lines()
        self.square = self.unit_square()

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)
        self.play(Create(self.grid), run_time=1.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.square, scale=0.7), run_time=0.9)

        lab = self.panel(
            VGroup(Text("area", font_size=20, color=DIM),
                   MathTex("1", font_size=30, color=AREA_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            Text("the unit of measure", font_size=18, color=DIM),
        )
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(l, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for l in lab],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.2))
        self.lab = lab
        self.wait(1.2)

    @beat("Transform it, and measure what you get", seconds=17,
          narration="Apply a map. The square becomes a slanted parallelogram, "
                    "and measuring it gives an area of five. Not approximately "
                    "five — exactly, and the same five you get from ad minus "
                    "bc: three times two, minus one times one.")
    def measure(self):
        assert verify_det_is_area_factor(M)
        after = polygon_area([M.apply(p) for p in
                              (Vec2(0, 0), Vec2(1, 0), Vec2(1, 1), Vec2(0, 1))])
        assert abs(after - M.det) < 1e-12 and abs(M.det - 5.0) < 1e-12

        self.play(FadeOut(self.lab), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(Transform(self.square, self.unit_square(M)), run_time=2.2)

        rows = self.panel(
            VGroup(Text("measured area", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{after:.0f}", font_size=28, color=AREA_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            MathTex(rf"ad - bc = {M.a:.0f}\cdot{M.d:.0f} - {M.b:.0f}\cdot{M.c:.0f}",
                    font_size=24, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"= {M.det:.0f}", font_size=30, color=AREA_C),
        )
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.8))
        self.rows = rows
        self.wait(1.4)

    @beat("It is the same factor for every shape", seconds=21,
          narration="And it is not special to the square. Take any shape at "
                    "all — this lopsided quadrilateral, chosen precisely "
                    "because it is not aligned to anything — and its area is "
                    "multiplied by the same five. That is what the determinant "
                    "is: one number saying how much the map stretches every "
                    "area there is.")
    def any_shape(self):
        before = abs(polygon_area(SHAPE))
        after = abs(polygon_area([M.apply(p) for p in SHAPE]))
        assert abs(after / before - abs(M.det)) < 1e-9

        self.play(FadeOut(self.rows), FadeOut(self.square), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(Transform(self.grid, self.axes_lines()), run_time=0.01)
        blob = self.blob()
        self.play(FadeIn(blob, scale=0.8), run_time=0.9)
        self.play(Transform(blob, self.blob(M)), run_time=2.2)

        rows = self.panel(
            VGroup(Text("before", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{before:.3f}", font_size=24, color=FLIP_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(Text("after", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{after:.3f}", font_size=24, color=FLIP_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(Text("ratio", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{after/before:.3f}", font_size=28, color=AREA_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
        )
```

```python
from manim import *

class StabilityInMotion(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Stability in Motion: The Tale of Numerical Integration", font_size=36)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title))
        
        # Introduction
        intro = Text("How do numerical methods affect stability?", font_size=30)
        self.play(Write(intro))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(intro))
        
        # Create axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=8,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False},
        )
        
        x_label = Text("Time", font_size=24).next_to(axes, DOWN)
        y_label = Text("Position", font_size=24).next_to(axes, LEFT)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Create the exact solution (simple oscillation)
        # Using simple points to create a sine-like curve
        t_values = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
        exact_points = []
        for t in t_values:
            exact_points.append(axes.c2p(t, np.cos(t)))
        
        exact_curve = VMobject(color=GREEN)
        exact_curve.set_points_smoothly(exact_points)
        exact_label = Text("Exact Solution", font_size=24, color=GREEN).to_edge(UP)
        
        self.play(Create(exact_curve), Write(exact_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Euler method (unstable) - oscillation with increasing amplitude
        euler_points = []
        for t in t_values:
            euler_points.append(axes.c2p(t, np.cos(t) * (1 + 0.15*t)))
        
        euler_curve = VMobject(color=RED)
        euler_curve.set_points_smoothly(euler_points)
        euler_label = Text("Euler Method (Unstable)", font_size=24, color=RED).next_to(exact_label, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(euler_curve), Write(euler_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Runge-Kutta (more stable) - less divergence
        rk_points = []
        for t in t_values:
            rk_points.append(axes.c2p(t, np.cos(t) * (1 + 0.05*t)))
        
        rk_curve = VMobject(color=BLUE)
        rk_curve.set_points_smoothly(rk_points)
        rk_label = Text("Runge-Kutta (More Stable)", font_size=24, color=BLUE).next_to(euler_label, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(rk_curve), Write(rk_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Verlet (very stable) - follows closely
        verlet_points = []
        for t in t_values:
            verlet_points.append(axes.c2p(t, np.cos(t) * (1 + 0.01*t)))
        
        verlet_curve = VMobject(color=GOLD)
        verlet_curve.set_points_smoothly(verlet_points)
        verlet_label = Text("Verlet (Very Stable)", font_size=24, color=GOLD).next_to(rk_label, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(verlet_curve), Write(verlet_label))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Fade everything out
        self.play(
            FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(x_label), FadeOut(y_label),
            FadeOut(exact_curve), FadeOut(euler_curve), FadeOut(rk_curve), FadeOut(verlet_curve),
            FadeOut(exact_label), FadeOut(euler_label), FadeOut(rk_label), FadeOut(verlet_label)
        )
        
        # Show equations
        eq_title = Text("Numerical Integration Methods", font_size=36)
        
        euler_eq = Text("Euler: y[n+1] = y[n] + h*f(t[n], y[n])", font_size=24, color=RED)
        rk_eq = Text("Runge-Kutta: y[n+1] = y[n] + h/6*(k1 + 2k2 + 2k3 + k4)", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        verlet_eq = Text("Verlet: y[n+1] = 2y[n] - y[n-1] + h^2*f(t[n], y[n])", font_size=24, color=GOLD)
        
        equations = VGroup(euler_eq, rk_eq, verlet_eq).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(eq_title))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(eq_title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        self.play(Write(euler_eq))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(rk_eq))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(verlet_eq))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Conclusion
        self.play(FadeOut(eq_title), FadeOut(euler_eq), FadeOut(rk_eq), FadeOut(verlet_eq))
        
        conclusion = Text("Stability depends on the chosen numerical method", font_size=36)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
```

```python
"""Gold scene 020 — the fewest colours that work.

Graphs, Tier 3. The scene exists to show a greedy algorithm being *wrong* --
not crashing, not obviously failing, but returning a valid answer that is one
colour worse than necessary, on a graph where nothing looks unusual.

The graph is a crown: three nodes on the left, three on the right, each joined
to the two opposite it but not the one across from it. Taken left-then-right
it takes two colours. Taken alternately it takes three. Same graph, same
algorithm, different order. ``chromatic_number`` settles which is right by
exhaustive search, so "one more than necessary" is a checked statement rather
than a claim about a picture.

That is the honest version of "NP-hard": not that the problem is impossible,
but that the cheap method can be beaten and knowing when costs you a search.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.graphs import (Graph, chromatic_number,
                                     greedy_colouring, verify_colouring)

PALETTE = ["#5CD0B3", "#F0AC5F", "#FC6255", "#8B7FD4"]
NODE_C = GREY_B
BAD_C = "#FC6255"
DIM = GREY_B

LAYOUT = LEFT * 2.0 + DOWN * 0.2
SC = 1.25

#: A crown graph: u_i joins every v_j except the one opposite it.
G = Graph(
    nodes={**{f"u{i}": (-1.5, 1.5 - i * 1.5) for i in range(3)},
           **{f"v{i}": (1.5, 1.5 - i * 1.5) for i in range(3)}},
    edges=[(f"u{i}", f"v{j}", 1.0)
           for i in range(3) for j in range(3) if i != j],
)

SIDE_FIRST = ["u0", "u1", "u2", "v0", "v1", "v2"]
ALTERNATING = ["u0", "v0", "u1", "v1", "u2", "v2"]


class GraphColouring(ForgeScene):

    def pos(self, n):
        x, y = G.nodes[n]
        return LAYOUT + np.array([x * SC, y * SC, 0.0])

    def panel(self, *rows):
        g = VGroup(*rows).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        return g.move_to(RIGHT * 4.2).align_to(UP * 2.4, UP)

    def build_nodes(self):
        self.circles, self.labels = {}, {}
        group = VGroup()
        for n in G.nodes:
            c = Circle(radius=0.28, color=NODE_C, stroke_width=2.6,
                       fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1.0).move_to(self.pos(n))
            t = Text(n, font_size=18, color=NODE_C).move_to(c)
            self.circles[n], self.labels[n] = c, t
            group.add(VGroup(c, t))
        return group

    def reset_colours(self):
        return [c.animate.set_fill(BLACK, opacity=1.0).set_stroke(NODE_C, width=2.6)
                for c in self.circles.values()] + \
               [t.animate.set_color(NODE_C) for t in self.labels.values()]

    def apply_order(self, order, run_time=0.55):
        """Colour the graph in ``order``, one node at a time, on screen."""
        colours = {}
        for n in order:
            used = {colours[m] for m, _ in G.neighbours(n) if m in colours}
            c = 0
            while c in used:
                c += 1
            colours[n] = c
            self.play(self.circles[n].animate.set_fill(
                          PALETTE[c], opacity=0.85).set_stroke(PALETTE[c], width=3.4),
                      self.labels[n].animate.set_color(BLACK),
                      run_time=run_time)
        # The on-screen result must equal what the primitive computes; if the
        # inline rule above ever drifts, the scene would narrate one thing and
        # show another.
        assert colours == greedy_colouring(G, order)
        assert verify_colouring(G, colours)
        return colours

    @beat("Colour the nodes so no edge joins two the same", seconds=20,
          narration="A network, and one rule: give every node a colour so "
                    "that no edge ever joins two nodes of the same colour. "
                    "This is timetabling in disguise — the nodes are exams, "
                    "the edges are students sitting both, and the colours are "
                    "time slots. Fewer colours means a shorter exam period.")
    def rule(self):
        self.title = Text("The fewest colours that work",
                          font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)

        self.edge_lines = {}
        lines = VGroup()
        for a, b, _ in G.edges:
            ln = Line(self.pos(a), self.pos(b), color=GREY_E, stroke_width=2.2)
            self.edge_lines[(a, b)] = ln
            lines.add(ln)
        nodes = self.build_nodes()

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(l) for l in lines],
                              lag_ratio=0.07, run_time=1.8))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(n, scale=0.6) for n in nodes],
                              lag_ratio=0.1, run_time=1.4))

        rule = self.panel(
            Text("rule", font_size=20, color=DIM),
            Text("joined nodes differ", font_size=23, color=PALETTE[0]),
            Text("goal", font_size=20, color=DIM),
            Text("use as few as possible", font_size=23, color=PALETTE[1]),
        )
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rule],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=2.0))
        self.rule_panel = rule
        self.wait(1.2)

    @beat("The obvious method: take the lowest colour that fits", seconds=20,
          narration="The obvious method is to go through the nodes one at a "
                    "time and give each the lowest-numbered colour none of "
                    "its neighbours has yet. It is fast, it never breaks the "
                    "rule, and here it finishes in two colours. Left side "
                    "green, right side amber, and every edge crosses between "
                    "them.")
    def greedy_good(self):
        self.play(FadeOut(self.rule_panel), run_time=0.4)

        label = Text("order: left side, then right", font_size=21,
                     color=DIM).next_to(self.title, DOWN, buff=0.32)
        self.play(FadeIn(label), run_time=0.6)

        colours = self.apply_order(SIDE_FIRST)
        used = len(set(colours.values()))

        result = self.panel(
            VGroup(MathTex(rf"{used}", font_size=40, color=PALETTE[0]),
                   Text("colours", font_size=21, color=DIM)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            Text("valid", font_size=20, color=PALETTE[0]),
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(result, shift=LEFT * 0.2), run_time=0.9)
        self.first_label, self.first_result = label, result
        self.first_used = used
        self.wait(1.4)

    @beat("Same graph, same method, a different order", seconds=22,
          narration="Now change nothing except the order. Take one node from "
                    "the left, then one from the right, and alternate. The "
                    "rule is applied exactly as before and the answer is "
                    "still valid — but it uses three colours instead of two. "
                    "The graph did not change. The algorithm did not change. "
                    "Only the order did.")
    def greedy_bad(self):
        self.play(FadeOut(self.first_result), *self.reset_colours(),
                  run_time=0.8)
        new_label = Text("order: alternating sides", font_size=21,
                         color=BAD_C).next_to(self.title, DOWN, buff=0.32)
        self.play(FadeTransform(self.first_label, new_label), run_time=0.6)

        colours = self.apply_order(ALTERNATING)
        used = len(set(colours.values()))
        assert used > self.first_used        # the point of the whole scene

        result = self.panel(
            VGroup(MathTex(rf"{used}", font_size=40, color=BAD_C),
                   Text("colours", font_size=21, color=DIM)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            Text("still valid", font_size=20, color=DIM),
            Text("still worse", font_size=22, color=BAD_C),
        )
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in result],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.6))
        self.second_label, self.second_result = new_label, result
        self.second_used = used
        self.wait(1.6)

    @beat("Knowing the true minimum means searching for it", seconds=26,
          narration="So which is right? Two is, and finding that out took a "
                    "search through every way of colouring the graph — "
                    "hundreds of assignments for six nodes, and rising as a "
                    "power of the number of nodes. That is the real shape of "
                    "the difficulty. A valid colouring is easy and a good one "
                    "is usually easy. Being certain you cannot do better is "
                    "what costs.")
    def hardness(self):
        chi = chromatic_number(G)
        assert chi == self.first_used
        assert chi < self.second_used

        self.play(FadeOut(self.second_result), FadeOut(self.second_label),
                  run_time=0.5)
        self.play(*self.reset_colours(), run_time=0.6)
        best = self.apply_order(SIDE_FIRST, run_time=0.32)
        assert len(set(best.values())) == chi

        n = len(G.nodes)
        rows = VGroup(
            VGroup(Text("greedy, good order", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{self.first_used}", font_size=28, color=PALETTE[0])
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(Text("greedy, bad order", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{self.second_used}", font_size=28, color=BAD_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(Text("true minimum", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{chi}", font_size=32, color=PALETTE[0])
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=DOWN),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.28, aligned_edge=LEFT)

        cost = VGroup(
            Text("to be sure, check", font_size=19, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"{chi}^{{{n}}} = {chi ** n}", font_size=28, color=DIM),
            Text("assignments", font_size=19, color=DIM),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2, aligned_edge=LEFT)

        panel = self.panel(rows, cost)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.8))
        self.play(FadeIn(cost, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(2.4)
```
